                    ### Question

She is at the 5th percentile for height and 80th percentile for weight. Physical examination shows a broad neck with bilateral excess skin folds that extend to the shoulders, as well as a low-set hairline and ears. There is an increased carrying angle when she fully extends her arms at her sides. Pulses are palpable in all extremities; lower leg pulses are delayed. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?

opb. Absent uterus

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of the 14-year-old girl, including short stature, broad neck with excess skin folds, low-set hairline and ears, increased carrying angle (cubitus valgus), and delayed lower leg pulses, is highly suggestive of Turner syndrome. Turner syndrome is characterized by features such as short stature, webbed neck, and cardiovascular anomalies like coarctation of the aorta, which can cause delayed lower leg pulses. A key finding in Turner syndrome is ovarian dysgenesis, leading to primary amenorrhea and infertility. The retrieved evidence path linking aortic symptoms to Turner's syndrome supports the association of cardiovascular anomalies with this condition. Therefore, the most likely additional finding in this patient is ovarian dysgenesis, consistent with the consensus on Turner syndrome.
